ratings_why.fun: Three real routes with a growth curve that kicks in at Foxfire and peaks at Aarnivalkea; you'd happily draft it, but early turns are thin bodies and the Drowning route leans on one card (Jack).
ratings_why.distinct: 8 over 7 because it wants empty slots: gaps are fuel for Flit, Foxfire, the Mapseller and the Clerk, and choosing them against the visible next board is a decision no current tribe or generic auto-battler tribe asks for.

verdict_why: The v2 rules read cleanly and the growth curve works; what's left is the owner's balancing and playtest calls, not a fix.

points.text: Glowing Barn Owl's once-a-fight +1/+1 is the thinnest T4 job next to Hoard-Keeper and Aarnivalkea; letting it trigger on any Drowned unit, or three times a fight, would make it a real Drowning buffer.
The Drowning route only kills reliably once Jack o' the Turnip arrives at T4; one smaller damage boost at T2 or T3 would give that route an earlier start.
Turns 1 to 4 are mostly dodges and one-off Astray with little permanent growth before Foxfire; a T1 seed that grows from Flits would give the fen line a first-turns hook.
Moon in the Mere's copied stats matter only when the lights attack, since lights go out before damage when hit; saying so on the card would help players read why it is a capstone.

standouts.why: Foxfire turns the gaps into a permanent curve and is the reason to keep the fen open late.
Fresh-Ink Mapseller uses gaps plus the visible next board to aim Astray at their Cleave or Bristle unit.
Old Will is a capstone the whole Astray stack builds to, and it adds to the small sources instead of replacing them.

weakest.why: Glowing Barn Owl: one +1/+1 packet a fight, gated on enemy Drownings only.
Little Phos does nothing when no enemy is across and its back-row mode is a coin flip.
Tiddy Mun is a fine number but only a bigger Fingerpost; it adds no new decision at T5.

flags.note: Old Will with Jack o' the Turnip (worse with either golden) can make a full enemy board's first wave kill itself; bounded per fight, but check it.
Aarnivalkea has no per-fight cap and counts both sides, so with Old Will, Jack and Moon's lights it can give many board-wide +1/+1s a fight.
Foxfire is about twice the T3 target on purpose, and a golden doubles that; linear, not a loop.
Hoard-Keeper's 3 gold a turn is a free unit a turn from T4 in the Drowning build.
